gloss: to emphasize; to stress; to highlight

definitions.gloss: to emphasize; to stress; to highlight the importance of something
definitions.explanation: Used when drawing special attention to a point, fact, or quality. Common in speeches, writing, presentations, and everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}の{重要性|じゅうようせい}を{強調|きょうちょう}する。
examples.english: To emphasize the importance of safety.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}はこの{点|てん}を{特|とく}に{強調|きょうちょう}した。
examples.english: The teacher particularly stressed this point.

examples.japanese: {大臣|だいじん}は{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}で{経済|けいざい}{対策|たいさく}の{必要性|ひつようせい}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}し{強調|きょうちょう}した。
examples.english: The minister repeatedly emphasized the need for economic measures at the press conference.

notes:
A very common word in both formal and informal contexts. Can refer to verbal emphasis (stressing a point) or visual emphasis (making text bold, using colors).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {強調|きょうちょう}{表示|ひょうじ}: highlighting (on screen)
- {強調|きょうちょう}{色|しょく}: highlight color
- ～を{強調|きょうちょう}する: to emphasize ~
- {特|とく}に{強調|きょうちょう}する: to particularly emphasize

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {重視|じゅうし}する: to attach importance to (focus on valuing, not communicating)
- {主張|しゅちょう}する: to assert, claim (stronger, implies arguing a position)
- {訴|うった}える: to appeal to (emotional persuasion)
